originality.rationale: Direct comparison of the accessible fixed-map CLT and the full same-family entropy paper found no triangular-array law or exact periodic curvature. The first theorem excludes the linear boundary and has map-dependent centering/variance; the other treats absolutely continuous invariant distributions, not unweighted periodic orbits. General parameter-response methods may enable derivations but do not state the same quantitative theorem. Priority remains subject to historical equivalence searches.

value.rationale: A naturally singular regime occurs as the positive variance of the fixed-map periodic CLT collapses to zero at the linear map. The critical n^-1/2 perturbation scale keeps both multiplier drift and orbit-to-orbit fluctuations finite, with explicit mean-variance relation and exact finite-period curvature for every degree. This addresses a motivated boundary of the source theorem and yields a transferable local statistic, not an arbitrary finite exercise.
